Jessica Watson (born 18 May 1993) is an Australian sailor who attempted a solo circumnavigation at the age of 16 from 18 October 2009 to 15 May 2010.
Whose son Bernardo became President of Guatemala in 2024, decades after this philosophy-professor-turned-statesman first won the office democratically in 1945?
Juan José Arévalo (10 September 1904 - 8 October 1990) was a Guatemalan statesman and professor of philosophy who became Guatemala's first democratically elected president in 1945.

This Dominican dictator, also nicknamed 'El Jefe,' ruled for 31 years via a personality cult and a feared secret police force until his 1961 assassination — who is he?
Rafael Trujillo: Dictator of the Dominican Republic from 1930 to 1961.

Fought from 1964 to 1979 in what would become independent Zimbabwe, this conflict pitted Ian Smith's white minority government against guerrilla forces led by Robert Mugabe and Joshua Nkomo — what was it called?
Rhodesian Bush War: 1964–1979 conflict in Southern Africa.
He founded Electronic Data Systems and never carried a single state, yet his 1992 and 1996 runs were among the strongest third-party showings in U.S. history — which Texan businessman was it?
Ross Perot: American businessman and politician (1930–2019)

A tailor's son turned Navy Board official and MP, he is remembered far less for his politics than for the candid private diary he kept for nearly a decade — a prime window into the Stuart Restoration. Who was he?
Samuel Pepys: English writer and politician (1633–1703)
Born in Leptis Magna in Roman Africa, this general emerged as the final victor of the chaotic Year of the Five Emperors to rule Rome from 193 to 211 — who is he?
Septimius Severus: Roman emperor from 193 to 211. Lucius Septimius Severus (Latin: [ˈluːkius sepˈtimius seˈweːrus]; 11 April 145 – 4 February 211) was Roman emperor from 193 to 211.
Fought in two stages, a winter and summer campaign from 1614 to 1615, this conflict ended the Toyotomi clan and cemented Tokugawa rule over Japan — which historic clash?
Siege of Osaka: 1614-15 series of battles in Japan at the end of the Sengoku Period.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.
A Thai Chinese general, he became the only king of Thonburi after leading the liberation of Siam from Burmese occupation and reuniting a country splintered among warlords — who was he?
Taksin: King of Siam from 1767 to 1782.
One of 24 Apollo astronauts to fly to the Moon, he commanded Apollo 10 and, with his crewmate, became the first to fly a Lunar Module in lunar orbit — which test pilot?
Thomas P. Stafford: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1930–2024)
This self-proclaimed Sapa Inca led a large Andean rebellion against Spanish colonial rule in Peru and later became a symbol of the independence movement — who was he?
Túpac Amaru II: Leader of an uprising in Peru.

His name became a byword for traitor, but this Norwegian officer once worked alongside explorer Fridtjof Nansen on famine relief before heading the Nazi puppet government during Germany's occupation of Norway — who is it?
Vidkun Quisling: Norwegian politician and Nazi collaborator (1887–1945)
Fought from 1879 to 1884 over nitrate-rich Atacama Desert territory, this conflict pitted Chile against an alliance of Bolivia and Peru, ending in a decisive Chilean victory — which conflict?
War of the Pacific: Territorial conflict between Chile and allied Peru and Bolivia (1879–84)

Despite a huge edge in tanks and aircraft, the Soviet Union took heavy losses and was expelled from the League of Nations after its November 1939 invasion of Finland — what was this three-and-a-half-month conflict called?
Winter War: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland.
A former steel-plant foundryman, this Soviet pilot orbited Earth once in 108 minutes aboard Vostok 1 and became an overnight global celebrity — who is he?
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Dorothea Klumpke is an astronomer. Dorothea Klumpke Roberts (August 9, 1861 in San Francisco – October 5, 1942 in San Francisco) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Georg Cantor is a mathematician. Cantor's method of proof of this theorem implies the existence of an infinity of infinities.
What is the atomic number of Thorium?
Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
What is the atomic number of Osmium?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
In what year was Scott Cawthon born?
Scott Cawthon: Cawthon began his career developing family-friendly Christian video games to minimal success.
In what year was Brian Cox born?
Brian Cox (physicist): Brian Edward Cox (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
In what year was Nikola Tesla born?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
In what year did Homi J. Bhabha die?
Homi J. Bhabha: Bhabha was awarded the Adams Prize (1942) and Padma Bhushan (1954), and nominated for the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1951 and 1953–1956.
In what year did Enrico Fermi die?
Enrico Fermi: With his colleagues, Fermi filed several patents related to the use of nuclear power, all of which were taken over by the US government.
In what year was Beryllium discovered?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
Eurocopter Tiger: Airbus Helicopters. The Eurocopter EC665 Tiger, is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter which first entered service in 2003.
In which country is Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: United Kingdom. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
Fufu: Ghana. Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine.
Who is credited with discovering Tennessine?
Tennessine: Yuri Oganessian. Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Who is credited with discovering Ammonia?
Ammonia: Joseph Priestley. Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Who is credited with discovering Selenium?
Selenium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
Despite overseeing Soviet thermonuclear weapons development, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his activism on human rights and individual freedom — who is he?
Andrei Sakharov (21 May 1921 - 14 December 1989) was a Soviet physicist and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, which he was awarded in 1975 for emphasizing human rights around the world.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Originating in Central Africa and classified as a hound by the American Kennel Club, this dog breed doesn't bark but instead makes an unusual yodel-like sound due to its uniquely shaped larynx — what's the breed?
Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.
A flowering vine native to South Asia, this plant's small dried red drupes become the world's most traded spice, its final coloring depending on how ripe the fruit was when harvested — which spice?
Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is a flowering vine in the family Piperaceae, cultivated for its fruit (the peppercorn), which is usually dried and used as a spice and seasoning.
Also known as undulant fever and Malta fever, this zoonotic illness spreads mainly through drinking unpasteurized milk and is caused by tiny coccobacilli — what is it?
Brucellosis is a zoonosis (zoonotic disease) spread primarily via ingestion of unpasteurized milk from infected animals.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.

Named from the Latin word for 'finger' because of its tubular, spike-borne flowers, this genus of about 20 European and West Asian species was reclassified into a new plant family in 2001 — what is it commonly called?
Digitalis (or) is a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous perennial plants, shrubs, and biennials, commonly called foxgloves.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints, stretchy velvety skin, and abnormal scarring, sometimes leading to aortic dissection — name the condition?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) are a group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders.
From abortion to animal welfare to business practices, the 'applied' branch of this philosophical study tackles real-world moral problems. What is it?
Ethics is the philosophical study of moral phenomena. Its main branches include normative ethics, applied ethics, and metaethics.
This everyday bodily process — expelling gas from the intestines through the anus — has its own dedicated field of scientific study named after it: what's the term for the process itself?
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines via the anus, commonly referred to as farting.
Its name comes from Greek words meaning "study of the earth," and this science examines the rocks and processes that shape not just our planet but other astronomical bodies too — what field is it?
Geology is a branch of natural science concerned with the Earth and other astronomical bodies, the rocks of which they are composed, and the processes by which they change over time.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
This medical condition occurs when the body, or a region of it, is deprived of adequate oxygen at the tissue level — what is it called?

Hypoxia (medicine) is a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of an adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxia may be classified as either generalized, affecting the whole body, or local, affecting a region of the body.

Once found as far north as Texas's Lower Rio Grande Valley but now extirpated from the US, this slender wild cat comes in gray and red color morphs, ranging from Mexico to Argentina — what animal is it?
Jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi); or is a wild cat native to the Americas.
This mammalogist survived a 3,000-meter fall strapped to her airplane seat after a 1971 lightning strike, then spent 11 days alone in the Amazon before rescue — who is she?
Juliane Koepcke (born 10 October 1954), is a German-Peruvian mammalogist who specialises in bats.
Native to the Mediterranean and prized for its fragrant purple blooms, this genus of some 47 flowering plant species belongs to the sage family — name it?
Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.

This American single-engine supersonic interceptor, designed by Kelly Johnson after interviewing Korean War fighter pilots, became part of the 'Century Series' and was widely used as a Cold War fighter-bomber. What is it?
Lockheed F-104 Starfighter is an American single-engine, supersonic interceptor. It was also produced under license by other nations and saw widespread service outside the United States.
A large canine of South America resembling a red fox in markings but being neither fox nor wolf. It's the only species in its genus and the largest canine in South America. What is it?
Maned wolf (Chrysocyon brachyurus) is a large canine of South America.
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride salt form as 'crystal meth' — what is it?

Methamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is primarily used as a recreational or performance-enhancing drug and less commonly as a second-line treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

Physicians in this medical specialty diagnose and surgically treat eye disorders — and can often spot signs of diseases elsewhere in the body just by examining a patient's eyes — what specialty is it?
Ophthalmology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of eye diseases and disorders.
This Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner coined the word 'conurbation' and his work contains one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally.' Who was he?
Patrick Geddes (2 October 1854 - 17 April 1932) was a Scottish biologist, sociologist, Comtean positivist, geographer, philanthropist and pioneering town planner.

First described in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the cellar spider and the "vibrating spider" — and lends the nickname "daddy long-legs" to one of its species; what is the family?
Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Ancient Chinese philosopher Confucius believed this oratorical skill could profoundly move even those not present in the room — what is the term for addressing a live audience?
Public speaking is the delivery of a speech to a live audience.
Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flow,' this umbrella term covers more than 200 different conditions causing chronic joint or connective-tissue pain, including arthritis — what's the term?
Rheumatism (from the Ancient Greek, rhema) or rheumatic disorders are conditions causing chronic, often intermittent pain affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Which genus of 20 to 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae produces both a fragrant white flower cluster and a dark berry, each with their own distinct common name?

Sambucus is a genus of between 20 and 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae. The various species are commonly referred to as elder, with the flowers as elderflower, and the fruit as elderberry.

Though many are crustaceans more closely related to insects than to fish, which group of exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates, including molluscs and echinoderms, is a leading cause of food allergies?
Shellfish are exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.
This birth defect involves incomplete closure of the spinal column and its surrounding membranes during early pregnancy, occurring in three recognized forms — what condition is it?
Spina bifida (SB; Latin for 'split spine') is a birth defect in which there is incomplete closing of the spine and the membranes around the spinal cord during early development in pregnancy.
Named for its long, flat, sword-like bill, this large migratory predatory fish loses all its teeth and scales by adulthood and is a popular target among billfish anglers — what is it?
Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis and treated with the antibiotic streptomycin, this tick-borne illness also goes by an animal-related nickname — what is it?
Tularemia is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.
The first woman ever to serve as Ukraine's prime minister, this politician held that post in 2005 and again from 2007 to 2010, and now leads the Batkivshchyna political party — who is she?

Yulia Tymoshenko (ne Hrihyan; born 27 November 1960) is a Ukrainian politician, who served as Prime Minister of Ukraine in 2005, and again from 2007 until 2010; the first woman in Ukraine to hold that position.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
A colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a famously pungent smell, this compound has about 70% of its industrial output turned into fertilisers — what is it?
Ammonia: Chemical compound. A stable binary hydride and the simplest pnictogen hydride, ammonia is a colourless gas with a distinctive pungent smell.
Caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis, its skin form starts as a small blister that becomes a painless ulcer with a telltale black center — what infection is this?
Anthrax: Infection caused by Bacillus anthracis bacteria. The skin form presents with a small blister with surrounding swelling that often turns into a painless ulcer with a black center.
Known as mugwort or wormwood, this daisy-family plant has long been used for both medicinal and culinary purposes — what species is it?

Artemisia vulgaris: Medicinal plant known as common mugwort. It is one of several species in the genus Artemisia commonly known as mugwort, although Artemisia vulgaris is the species most often called mugwort.
Blooming for weeks each spring and thriving in the shade under trees, these flowering shrubs belong to the genus Rhododendron — what are they called?
Azalea: Subgroup of rhododendron flowering shrubs.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
Native to tropical South America, this large non-venomous member of family Boidae is a fixture of private collections thanks to its wildly variable color patterns — what species is it?
Known for a widely viewed 2010 TEDx talk on shame and vulnerability, which academic wrote six consecutive number-one New York Times bestsellers, including Daring Greatly?
Brené Brown: American academic, speaker and author.
Found in chalk, limestone, eggshells, and pearls alike, this CaCO3 compound is also the active ingredient in agricultural lime and doubles as an antacid — what is it?
Calcium carbonate: Chemical compound. Materials containing much calcium carbonate or resembling it are described as calcareous.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
Making up a quarter to a third of all protein in mammals, this triple-helix fibrous protein needs vitamin C for its synthesis and gives structure to cartilage, tendons, and skin — what is it?
Collagen: Most abundant structural protein in animals.
Home to crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, this bird family boasts a brain-to-body ratio rivaling great apes, and one of its members even passed the mirror self-recognition test — what family is this?

A Scottish biologist, classicist and mathematician who pioneered theoretical biology, he's remembered for his 1917 book On Growth and Form, which opened the way to explaining how patterns and body structures take shape — who was he?
D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson: Scottish biologist, mathematician, and classics scholar.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a single day, this condition is most often caused by an intestinal infection from contaminated food or water — what is it?

Diarrhea: Loose or liquid bowel movements. Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
Element 105 sparked a long Cold War naming dispute, claimed first by a Soviet institute in 1968 and then by Berkeley in 1970 before being settled in 1993 — which synthetic element?
Dubnium: Chemical element with atomic number 105 (Db)
The second-largest member of the deer family, this animal is also called "wapiti," a Shawnee and Cree word meaning "white rump" for the pale fur it flashes to signal alarm — what animal is it?
Elk: Species of deer. The word "elk" originally referred to the European variety of the moose, Alces alces, but was transferred to Cervus canadensis by North American colonists.

In 2019 this French-American MIT economist shared the Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty, rooted in the randomized trials of her J-PAL lab — who is she?

Recognized by their pod-like fruit and compound leaves, this plant family — the third-largest among flowering plants — includes beans, peas, and lentils along with genera like Acacia and Mimosa. What family is it?
Fabaceae: Family of legume flowering plants. Fabaceae or Leguminosae, commonly known as the legume, pea, or bean family, is a large and agriculturally important family of flowering plants.
This whip-like appendage propels sperm cells and lets bacteria like Helicobacter pylori swim through stomach mucus, sometimes triggering ulcers — what is it called?
Flagellum: Cellular appendage functioning as locomotive or sensory organelle.

Unlike plants, this kingdom of life can't photosynthesize, and unlike most things, it has chitin in its cell walls — feeding instead by oozing digestive enzymes out and absorbing what dissolves. What group includes yeasts, molds, and mushrooms?
Fungus: Organism belonging to kingdom Fungi.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?
This large, widely distributed white wading bird nests in colonies built in trees near water and is now expanding its range into northern Europe — which species?
Great egret: Species of bird. The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.
A young one of this fast-running lagomorph is called a leveret, and a group of them may be known as a 'husk' or a 'down'?
Hare: Genus of mammals in the family Leporidae.
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.
Traditionally drawn from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this blue compound is the color most associated with denim and blue jeans — what is it?
Indigo dye: Chemical compound, food additive and dye.
This American climatologist's 1988 Congressional testimony helped awaken the public to global warming, and he later turned activist — getting arrested more than once for the cause. Who is it?

Born John Chapman, this American pioneer nurseryman planted seed-grown apple trees across Pennsylvania, Ohio and beyond, becoming a folk hero in his own lifetime for his kindness and conservation. By what nickname do we know him?
A pastor's son and theoretical physicist, this man passed Manhattan Project secrets to the Soviets, served nine years in a British prison, then resumed his science career in East Germany. Who is he?
Klaus Fuchs: German-born British physicist and atomic spy (1911–1988)
A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange, this small evergreen tree may have first appeared in northeastern India, and its fruit's juice is about 5–6% citric acid — what is it?

This anatomic form of lung infection causes inflammatory fluid to consolidate across an entire continuous section of one lung, and in children shows up instead as a rounded pattern due to immature air-pore connections — what is it?
Lobar pneumonia: Lung infection. It is one of three anatomic classifications of pneumonia (the other being bronchopneumonia and atypical pneumonia).
A field of artificial intelligence built on statistics and optimization, it develops algorithms that learn from data and handle unseen examples without being explicitly programmed — what is it?
Machine learning: Subset of artificial intelligence. Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning.

In 1835 this Scottish polymath and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and she signed first on John Stuart Mill's 1866 petition for women's suffrage — who was she?

Diagnosed when a person has at least three of five red flags -- including abdominal obesity and high blood pressure -- this cluster of conditions raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes in about a quarter of US adults. What is it?
Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of diseases occurring with obesity.
Developed in Germany in the late 1800s from the smallest members of a larger breed to create an efficient ratter, this pint-sized dog remains one of the most popular breeds worldwide — which breed?
Miniature Schnauzer: German breed of dog. Miniature Schnauzers are recognized in four colors internationally: solid black, black and silver, salt and pepper, and white.
This cancer attacks plasma cells — the white blood cells that normally make antibodies — often silently at first before bringing bone pain, anemia, and kidney trouble. What is it?
Multiple myeloma: Cancer of plasma cells. There is an increased risk of multiple myeloma in certain occupations, due to occupational exposure to aromatic hydrocarbon solvents.
Also called roundworms, these mostly free-living animals have a tubular digestive tract with openings at both ends and are grouped with arthropods in the clade Ecdysozoa — what are they?

Introduced in 2001 and originally developed under the name Tier II+, which remotely piloted, high-altitude surveillance aircraft supports the US Air Force with long-endurance radar and infrared sensors?
Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk: Unmanned surveillance aircraft. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.

Traditionally eaten whole in French cuisine, with diners often covering their heads with a napkin while doing so, this small Eurasian songbird's population crashed from overhunting despite EU protection — which bird?
Ortolan bunting: Species of bird in Eurasia.
Strong curved beak, upright stance, clawed feet — this order of roughly 410 tropical bird species, including the cockatoos, faces a higher extinction risk than any comparable bird group — what is it?
Parrot: Order of birds. One-third of all parrot species are threatened by extinction, with a higher aggregate extinction risk (IUCN Red List Index) than any other comparable bird group.
Characterized by an enduring, inflexible pattern of behavior and thinking that deviates from social norms, this mental health classification impairs relationships and self-concept?
Personality disorder: Maladaptive patterns of behavior, cognition, and inner experience.
Linked to prolonged sitting and excess hair, which skin condition causes a cyst to form between the cheeks of the buttocks and is treated with incision and drainage?
Pilonidal disease: Skin infection between the buttocks. Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Soft enough to slice with a knife, this silvery alkali metal carries the symbol K and takes its name from potash, the plant ashes it was first isolated from — what element is it?
Potassium: Chemical element with atomic number 19 (K)
This emotional response to severe distressing events like violence or a life-threatening injury can trigger flashbacks, panic attacks, insomnia, and post-traumatic stress disorder — what's it called?
Psychological trauma: Emotional response caused by severe distressing events.
This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species includes the buttercups, spearworts, and water crowfoots — which genus?
Ranunculus: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family.
Its seeds yield castor oil but also harbor a highly potent toxin — which plant genus, better known for producing the castor bean?
Ricinus: Monotypic genus of plant in the spurge family.
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.

Starting from stem cells near the wall of the seminiferous tubules, this multi-stage process runs cells through two rounds of meiosis to turn diploid germ cells into haploid swimmers. What is it called?
Usually caused by Staphylococcus bacteria and treated at home with warm compresses, this tender red bump at the edge of the eyelid is also known as a hordeolum — what is it?
Stye: Swelling of the eyelid due to infection of an oil gland.
Despite over a thousand species of this large hairy spider, many popular pet varieties defend themselves with irritating urticating hairs rather than a dangerous bite — which arachnid?
Deaf from childhood and largely self-taught, this American began as a railroad telegrapher tinkering with telegraph systems before becoming a legendary inventor — who was he?
